medications.name: Oxycodone
medications.reason_stopped: Fogginess and constipation; pain was manageable on paracetamol and ibuprofen by then. About eleven days of use.

medications.name: Cephalexin
medications.dose: 500mg four times daily for seven days
medications.reason_stopped: Full course completed for a superficial wound infection.

symptoms.frequency: 8/10 at surgery, 7/10 by 2026-04-17, 5/10 through the wound infection, 3/10 by 2026-06-04, 2/10 from 2026-07-25 and only after a long day

symptoms.description: Evening swelling of the operated knee
symptoms.frequency: Marked early, now mild and confined to the evenings four months post-operatively

symptoms.description: Wound redness, warmth and yellowish discharge with temperature 37.9
symptoms.frequency: Single episode, treated with cephalexin, resolved within five days of starting

patterns_to_raise.observation: Knee flexion tracked physiotherapy adherence directly and measurably. Twice-daily exercises took flexion from 75 degrees on 2026-05-13 to 88 by 2026-05-28. Roughly three weeks of missed sessions after returning to work on 2026-06-11 saw it fall to 82 by 2026-06-26. Resuming twice daily on 2026-07-03 recovered it to 90 by 2026-07-10 and 105 by 2026-08-24.
patterns_to_raise.why_it_matters: A documented regression and recovery in the same patient, which the patient themselves connected at the time.

patterns_to_raise.observation: The wound infection was identified the day after the patient reported increasing redness, warmth, discharge and a temperature of 37.9 on 2026-04-28, and was treated the same day it was assessed. Redness had pulled back by day five of cephalexin.
patterns_to_raise.why_it_matters: Shows a short interval between the patient noticing a change and it being assessed, which is relevant context for how promptly this patient reports problems.

open_items.item: Whether evening swelling is expected this far post-operatively.
Return immediately if wound redness spreads or a fever develops.
Physiotherapy exercises once daily is appropriate at this stage.
